tie_reference: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: TIE.
source_note: Verified Chemistry Form One lesson plans (Arusha Catholic Seminary). 20 lesson plans (80 min double periods, 2 per week) covering Introduction to Chemistry (Week 1), Laboratory Rules and Safety (Week 2), First Aid & Apparatus (Week 3), Fire & Flames (Week 5), Flame Structure & Firefighting (Week 6), States of Matter (Week 7), Physical & Chemical Changes (Week 8), Elements & Symbols (Week 9), Compounds & Mixtures (Week 10), and Separating Mixtures (Week 11).

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 1: EXPLAIN THE CONCEPT AND BRANCHES OF CHEMISTRY
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of foundational chemistry concepts
lessons.specific_competence: 1.1 Define chemistry and its branches
lessons.main_activity: Explain the concept and branches of chemistry
lessons.specific_activity: Define chemistry; classify its branches (organic, inorganic, physical, analytical, biochemistry) with examples of what each studies
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners what images come to mind when they hear "chemistry"; records responses on the board.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share initial ideas in a quick brainstorm.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Defines chemistry formally; introduces the five branches with the classification chart, giving one real-world example per branch.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; copy branch chart into notebooks.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Organises a concept-mapping activity where groups place given topics (e.g., "rusting," "digestion," "rocket fuel") under the correct branch.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Work in groups to build a concept map matching topics to branches.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct placement of topics under branches

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions asking learners to justify their group's placements.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 2: INTERDISCIPLINARY LINKS AND APPLICATIONS OF CHEMISTRY
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of foundational chemistry concepts
lessons.specific_competence: 1.2–1.3 Explain chemistry's links with other disciplines and its applications
lessons.main_activity: Explain the interdisciplinary links and applications of chemistry
lessons.specific_activity: Link chemistry to Biology, Physics, Mathematics, Geography, and Agriculture; discuss applications of chemistry in medicine, agriculture, industry, and careers
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Interdisciplinary chart, career flashcards, industry pictures
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps Period 1's branches briefly; asks how a Biology teacher might also use chemistry.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall previous lesson; give a guess.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains, with the interdisciplinary chart, how chemistry links to each subject; shows industry pictures illustrating applications.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct identification of at least 3 links

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Assigns groups a career flashcard (doctor, farmer, engineer, forensic officer) and asks them to prepare a 2-minute case study on how that career uses chemistry.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Discuss in groups; prepare and present a short case study.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Quality and accuracy of group presentation

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Facilitates whole-class discussion comparing the presentations; administers the Chapter 1 Review Test.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Listen to peers; complete review test.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 3: LABORATORY RULES AND HAZARD SYMBOLS
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of laboratory safety and practices
lessons.specific_competence: 2.1 Explain laboratory rules and hazard symbols
lessons.main_activity: Explain laboratory rules, dress code, and hazard symbols
lessons.specific_activity: State laboratory rules and correct dress code; identify hazard symbols (toxic, corrosive, flammable, irritant)
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Lab safety poster, PPE samples, hazard symbol charts
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks what could go wrong entering a lab without following any rules.
Conducts a lab tour/demonstration explaining each safety rule and correct PPE use.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration; try on PPE samples; record rules.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct listing of at least 5 rules

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Runs a hazard-symbol matching game: groups match symbol cards to their meaning and an example substance.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Play matching game in groups; justify matches.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Distributes a rules checklist for learners to self-assess their understanding.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 4: SAFE CHEMICAL HANDLING AND FIRST AID PROCEDURES
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of laboratory safety and practices
lessons.specific_competence: 2.2 Explain safe chemical handling and first aid procedures
lessons.main_activity: Explain safe handling/storage/disposal of chemicals and first aid response
lessons.specific_activity: Describe safe handling, storage, and disposal of chemicals; explain first aid for cuts, burns, chemical splashes, and poisoning
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: First aid box/kit, PPE samples, lab safety poster
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps hazard symbols from Period 1; asks what to do if acid splashes on skin.
Demonstrates safe handling, storage, and disposal procedures for common lab chemicals.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration; note key safety steps.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Leads a first-aid role play: groups act out responding to a cut, a burn, a chemical splash, and suspected poisoning.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform role play in groups, applying correct first aid steps.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Observes and scores each group's practical response using a checklist.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 5: FIRST AID KIT CONTENTS AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of laboratory safety and practices
lessons.specific_competence: 2.2 Identify first aid kit contents and emergency procedures
lessons.main_activity: Apply first aid kit use in emergencies
lessons.specific_activity: Identify first aid kit contents (bandages, antiseptic, gloves, scissors, eyewash) and describe the correct emergency procedure for each type of injury
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: First aid kit, lab safety poster
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Opens the first aid kit and asks learners to name any items they recognise.
Explains the use of each item and the correct emergency sequence (assess, protect, treat, refer).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe; take notes on procedure sequence.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a practical demonstration where groups practice locating and using specific kit items for a given scenario card.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Practice using kit items per scenario in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews with rapid-fire oral questions on which item suits which injury.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 6: BASIC CHEMISTRY LABORATORY APPARATUS
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of laboratory safety and practices
lessons.specific_competence: 2.3 Identify basic chemistry laboratory apparatus
lessons.main_activity: Identify and use basic laboratory apparatus
lessons.specific_activity: Identify test tubes, beakers, flasks, funnels, burettes, Bunsen burner, tripod stand, wire gauze, measuring cylinder, pipette, thermometer, and balance; state the use of each
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Real laboratory apparatus, apparatus charts, measuring instruments
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Displays 3–4 pieces of apparatus and asks learners to guess their names/uses.
Introduces each remaining apparatus item, stating its name, use, and safe handling.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe; label a diagram sheet as items are introduced.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Runs an apparatus identification and measurement drill in groups (measuring set volumes with cylinder/pipette, reading a thermometer, using a balance).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Rotate through stations identifying apparatus and taking measurements.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers an apparatus identification test with labelled diagrams.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Apparatus Identification Test / Diagram Labeling Test score

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 7: CONCEPT AND CONDITIONS FOR FIRE
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of fire, flames, and firefighting
lessons.specific_competence: 3.1 Explain the concept and conditions for fire
lessons.main_activity: Explain fire, the fire triangle, and its causes/effects
lessons.specific_activity: Define fire and the fire triangle (fuel, heat, oxygen); discuss causes and effects of fire using real case studies
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Fire triangle chart, case studies/news clippings
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners the three things needed to start and sustain a fire.
Explains the fire triangle and demonstrates removing one element to show a fire dies (e.g., smothering a candle).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration; label the fire triangle diagram.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Distributes case studies/news clippings on real fire incidents; groups identify the fuel, heat source, and effects in each case.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Analyse case studies in groups; discuss findings.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Leads whole-class sharing of case study findings and clarifies misconceptions.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 8: CLASSIFICATION OF FIRES AND TYPES OF FLAMES
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of fire, flames, and firefighting
lessons.specific_competence: 3.1–3.2 Classify fires and explain the concept of flames
lessons.main_activity: Classify fires and distinguish types of flames
lessons.specific_activity: Classify fires into classes A, B, C, D, and electrical; define flame and distinguish luminous from non-luminous flames using the Bunsen burner
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the fire triangle; asks if all fires are put out the same way.
Explains the five fire classes with examples of each fuel type, using the fire class chart.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; match examples to classes.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Demonstrates the Bunsen burner with air-hole open and closed; groups record observations of luminous vs non-luminous flames.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration in groups; record flame characteristics.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers a fire classification test.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 9: FLAME STRUCTURE AND ZONES
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of fire, flames, and firefighting
lessons.specific_competence: 3.2 Describe flame structure
lessons.main_activity: Describe the zones of a non-luminous flame
lessons.specific_activity: Identify and describe the three zones of a non-luminous Bunsen flame (dark zone, luminous zone, outer/hottest zone)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks which part of a candle flame is hottest and why they think so.
Draws and explains the three flame zones on the board using the flame structure diagram.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Copy and label the flame diagram.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Demonstrates testing the temperature of each zone (e.g., holding a matchstick briefly across the flame) for groups to observe and record.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration in groups; record which zone chars the matchstick fastest.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews with a diagram-based matching exercise on flame zones.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 10: FIREFIGHTING METHODS AND EQUIPMENT
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of fire, flames, and firefighting
lessons.specific_competence: 3.3 Explain methods and equipment used in firefighting
lessons.main_activity: Explain firefighting methods, equipment, and prevention
lessons.specific_activity: Explain cooling, smothering, starving, and chain-reaction-interruption methods; identify fire extinguisher types and their appropriate use; discuss fire prevention measures
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Firefighting method chart, sample extinguishers, fire prevention posters
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks how learners would put out a small kitchen fire at home.
Explains the four firefighting methods, linking each to the fire triangle; introduces extinguisher types and their matching fire classes.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; match extinguisher types to fire classes.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides groups in an equipment identification drill using sample extinguishers, followed by designing a fire-prevention poster/slogan for the school.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Identify extinguishers in groups; design a poster/slogan.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers an identification test on methods and equipment.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 11: STATES OF MATTER AND PARTICLE THEORY
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of the states and changes of matter
lessons.specific_competence: 4.1 Explain the states of matter and particle theory
lessons.main_activity: Explain matter, its states, and particle arrangement
lessons.specific_activity: Define matter; describe properties of solids, liquids, and gases; explain particle arrangement and movement using the kinetic theory
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows ice, water, and an inflated balloon; asks what is common and different among them.
Defines matter; explains properties of the three states and demonstrates particle arrangement using the bead model.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe bead model demonstration; take notes.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct description of particle arrangement per state

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides groups to handle the solid/liquid/gas samples and complete a property-comparison table (shape, volume, compressibility).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Handle samples; complete comparison table in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews with a diagram labeling test on particle arrangement.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 12: CHANGES OF STATE
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of the states and changes of matter
lessons.specific_competence: 4.1 Explain changes of state
lessons.main_activity: Explain melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, and sublimation
lessons.specific_activity: Describe melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, and sublimation; explain factors affecting the rate of change of state (temperature, surface area, pressure)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps particle arrangement briefly; asks what happens to ice left in the sun.
Demonstrates ice melting and water boiling, naming each change of state as it occurs.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration; record each change and its name.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a guided discussion and data-table activity on factors affecting rate of change (comparing melting times under different conditions).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Complete data table in groups; discuss factors.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Sets a cycle-diagram labeling task showing all changes of state in sequence.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 13: PHYSICAL CHANGE
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of the states and changes of matter
lessons.specific_competence: 4.2 Explain physical change
lessons.main_activity: Identify and explain physical changes
lessons.specific_activity: Define physical change; demonstrate and identify examples (cutting paper, melting ice, dissolving salt/sugar in water)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Tears a piece of paper in front of the class and asks if it is still paper.
Defines physical change; explains why cutting, melting, and dissolving are physical (no new substance formed).
Guides groups through practical stations: cutting paper, observing ice melt, dissolving salt/sugar in water.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform each activity in groups; record observations.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Leads discussion confirming each activity is reversible/no new substance formed.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 14: CHEMICAL CHANGE AND COMPARISON
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of the states and changes of matter
lessons.specific_competence: 4.2 Explain and apply chemical change
lessons.main_activity: Identify chemical changes and compare them with physical changes
lessons.specific_activity: Define chemical change with examples (burning, rusting, cooking); identify signs of a chemical reaction; compare physical and chemical change; apply to real-life situations
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Rusted nail sample, candle, comparison chart
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a rusted nail and asks if it can be turned back into shiny metal.
Defines chemical change; explains signs of reaction (colour change, gas production, heat, new substance) using the burning candle as a live example.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe candle burning; take notes on signs of reaction.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct listing of signs of reaction

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides groups to build a T-chart comparing physical vs chemical change using examples from both lessons, then apply the concept to real-life scenarios (cooking, rusting cars).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Build T-chart in groups; discuss real-life applications.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers the signs-of-reaction checklist and Chapter Review Test.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Signs-of-Reaction Checklist / Chapter Review Test score

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 15: ELEMENTS AND CHEMICAL SYMBOLS
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of elements, compounds, and mixtures
lessons.specific_competence: 5.1 Classify elements and apply chemical symbols
lessons.main_activity: Define elements and apply chemical symbol rules
lessons.specific_activity: Define an element; classify metals, non-metals, and metalloids; state chemical symbols and the rules for writing them
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a metal spoon and a piece of sulfur; asks how they differ.
Defines an element; explains classification into metals, non-metals, metalloids using the periodic table; states symbol-writing rules (capital first letter, lowercase second).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; identify sample elements on the periodic table.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Runs a symbol memorization drill and sample-sorting activity in groups (sorting samples into metal/non-metal/metalloid trays).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort samples in groups; practice writing symbols correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers a short symbol quiz.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 16: PROPERTIES AND USES OF ELEMENTS
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of elements, compounds, and mixtures
lessons.specific_competence: 5.1 Compare properties and uses of elements
lessons.main_activity: Compare properties of elements and describe their uses
lessons.specific_activity: Compare properties of elements (lustre, electrical conductivity, malleability); describe practical uses of common elements
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps metal/non-metal classification; asks why wires are made of copper, not wood.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall previous lesson; give a reason.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains lustre, conductivity, and malleability as distinguishing properties, demonstrating a conductivity test.
Guides groups to practically test conductivity of different samples and study use-case cards on real applications (aluminium in cans, copper in wiring, iron in construction).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Test conductivity in groups; discuss use-case studies.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Facilitates a group presentation on one element's properties and uses.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 17: CONCEPT OF COMPOUNDS
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of elements, compounds, and mixtures
lessons.specific_competence: 5.2 Explain the concept of compounds
lessons.main_activity: Explain compound formation from elements
lessons.specific_activity: Define a compound; explain how compounds form from elements chemically combining, using water and carbon dioxide as examples
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners to name a substance made of more than one element.
Defines a compound; explains formation from elements using the compound formation chart (e.g., hydrogen + oxygen → water).
Guides group discussion identifying more compound examples and their constituent elements from given substance cards.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Identify constituent elements of given compounds in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions reviewing compound formation.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 18: MIXTURES AND COMPARISON WITH COMPOUNDS
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of elements, compounds, and mixtures
lessons.specific_competence: 5.2 Explain mixtures and compare with compounds
lessons.main_activity: Explain mixtures and compare them with compounds
lessons.specific_activity: Define a mixture (homogeneous/heterogeneous); compare compounds and mixtures by composition, properties, and separability; classify given substances
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Sand/salt/water, comparison chart, sample substance cards
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps compounds; shows a cup of sand and water and asks if it's a compound.
Defines mixture types (homogeneous/heterogeneous) and explains differences from compounds (no fixed ratio, physically combined, separable).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; observe sand+water and salt+water examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a practical mixing activity (sand+water, salt+water) followed by building a T-chart comparing compounds and mixtures.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Mix substances in groups; complete T-chart.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Sets a classification worksheet using sample substance cards.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 19: SEPARATION METHODS - FILTRATION, DECANTATION, EVAPORATION, CRYSTALLIZATION
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of elements, compounds, and mixtures
lessons.specific_competence: 5.3 Explain filtration, decantation, evaporation, and crystallization
lessons.main_activity: Explain and demonstrate simple separation methods
lessons.specific_activity: Describe and practically demonstrate filtration, decantation, evaporation, and crystallization as methods of separating mixtures
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks how one would separate sand from water at home.
Explains filtration, decantation, evaporation, and crystallization, describing when each is appropriate.
Demonstrates filtration (sand from water) and evaporation (salt from water) practically; groups observe and record each step.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe and assist demonstration in groups; record observations.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews with oral questions comparing the four methods.

lessons.title: CHEMISTRY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 20: SEPARATION METHODS - DISTILLATION, SUBLIMATION, MAGNETIC SEPARATION
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of elements, compounds, and mixtures
lessons.specific_competence: 5.3 Explain distillation, sublimation, and magnetic separation; select appropriate methods
lessons.main_activity: Explain and apply distillation, sublimation, and magnetic separation
lessons.specific_activity: Describe distillation, sublimation, and magnetic separation; select the appropriate separation method for a given mixture
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Chemistry for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps filtration/evaporation briefly; asks how to separate iron filings from sand.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall previous lesson; predict a method.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains distillation using the diagram; demonstrates sublimation (if a suitable substance is available) and magnetic separation of iron filings from sand.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct diagram labeling of distillation set-up

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Sets a decision-matrix exercise where groups are given mixture cards and must select and justify the correct separation method for each.
Administers the Chapter Review Test covering all separation methods.
